# Embassy v1.6.0 — restarts survived, authority earned

The headline is the wedge that's gone: **an App Server restart no longer strands your Codex routes until you restart the broker.** Endpoint-transition evidence now survives to be claimed exactly once, queued mail carries its authority across the generation change, and — the piece that mattered most in live testing — recovery re-arms on the actual stale-to-healthy edge instead of burning a finite retry burst into silence. When the blocker is on your side of the seam (the Desktop app attaches to the managed daemon only at launch), the dashboard now says so, with the exact relaunch command.

The second story is the beginning of **authority earned by demonstration rather than version trust**. Embassy's evidence ladder always said a build should be writable "only where probes cover writes" — as of this release, that clause is satisfiable. An optional write-attestation probe can create one disposable, broker-owned, fully fenced thread, run one bounded turn on the pinned model at its lowest advertised effort, verify the pin was honored, archive the thread, and confirm it gone — recording write-covering evidence that, deliberately, unlocks nothing yet. In its first live run the entire attestation cost 17,942 tokens and left exactly one archived thread. Every published security claim was rewritten to state this precisely; no surface still promises "never `turn/start`."

Around those two: compatibility surfaces can now be optional (a missing provider renders "Not detected" instead of refusing to boot), a locally installed **DeepSeek harness appears on your diagnostics table** — detected by attestation, never launched, honestly quarantined until a stable release exists to certify — and version evidence learned to represent prerelease builds truthfully: attestable, never writable, with 0.x series treated per-minor because upstream treats them as breaking.

Verification for this release: 833 tests (up 75), soak clean, every slice independently gated from an isolated worktree, two adversarial review rounds plus a taste review on the largest change, and the fixes proven against a live daemon restart. One honest limit: the full slow-reattach drill validated the guidance surfaces live, and the re-arm fix is proven by reproduction tests; the end-to-end drill on the final build runs as this release's live proof.

Upgrade: `npm install -g agent-embassy@1.6.0`, restart your broker. If your ChatGPT Desktop was open across a daemon restart, relaunch it with `/usr/bin/open --env CODEX_APP_SERVER_USE_LOCAL_DAEMON=1 -a ChatGPT`.
